audits.title: 1008 Management of Suspected Testicular Torsion – Audit of Current Practice
audits.standard: NCEPOD and GIRFT recommendations for suspected testicular torsion

cycle1.result: 53.1% (n=17) reviewed by surgical team within 1 hour; 37.5% (n=12) explored within 1 hour of review; torsion in 21.8% (n=7), 3 (42.8%) needed orchidectomy.

audits.intervention: Data presented at local governance meeting and a new clinical pathway created.
audits.other_findings: Post-pathway data are said to have been collected and analysed but are not reported; 7 patients (21.8%) re-presented after surgery.
audits.citation: Stuart-Delavaine C, Frackleton R, Willis K. 1008 Management of Suspected Testicular Torsion – Audit of Current Practice. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.415.

audits.title: 698 Rate of Testicular Torsion and Variations in Operative Techniques for Scrotal Exploration - a Single Centre Audit
audits.setting: Grange University Hospital, Newport, general surgical unit

cycle1.result: 4/41 (9.8%) had confirmed testicular torsion. 33 of those without torsion (89.2%) underwent orchidopexy; most orchidopexies were 3-point fixation with PDS (66.7%).

audits.intervention: Local intervention aiming for consensus (details not stated); second cycle planned
audits.other_findings: Transverse (43.9%) and longitudinal para-median (41.5%) incisions were the most common; practice varied among general surgeons.
audits.citation: Baker W, Dermanis A, Pollitt J. 698 Rate of Testicular Torsion and Variations in Operative Techniques for Scrotal Exploration - a Single Centre Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.267.

audits.title: TTP7.14 Audit of Management of Testicular Torsion in a Rural General Hospital
audits.standard: Available national and international guidelines on testicular torsion
audits.setting: Bronglais General Hospital, Aberystwyth, rural general hospital managed by on-call general surgeons

cycle1.result: 13 had torsion; 4 of these had a non-viable testis, 3 of whom presented late (1-3 days after onset).

audits.intervention: Local protocol being developed with direct referral to on-call surgical registrar and TWIST score.
audits.other_findings: Management judged timely; raising awareness among children and carers is emphasised.
audits.citation: Mohamed S, Mohammed S, Ali M, Aniah M, Kanagaraj S, Stolarchuk T. TTP7.14 Audit of Management of Testicular Torsion in a Rural General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.307.

audits.title: 154 Recovering From Multiple Missed Torsions: A Service Improvement in a District General Hospital
audits.standard: Timely surgery for suspected testicular torsion with TWIST score risk stratification
audits.setting: Wexham Park Hospital, district general hospital (ED and urology)

cycle1.result: Mean time to theatre 276 minutes from ED presentation and 200 minutes from decision-to-operate; TWIST score calculated in 3.6% of cases.

audits.intervention: New torsion pathway in 2023: expedited referral from triage, electronic TWIST-based risk stratification tool, and targeted ED and urology education.

cycle2.result: Mean time to theatre 162 minutes from presentation and 100 minutes from decision-to-operate; TWIST documented in 75%.

audits.other_findings: Prompted by five missed torsions in 2021-2022; no missed torsions from implementation to re-audit, and TWIST ≥5 predicted torsion in all cases.
audits.citation: Krum T, Othman Z, Ibrahim M, Choo L, Forster L. 154 Recovering From Multiple Missed Torsions: A Service Improvement in a District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.735.

audits.title: Audit of Compliance With BURST-BAUS FIX-IT Guidelines for Scrotal Exploration in Suspected Testicular Torsion: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: BURST-BAUS FIX-IT consensus guidelines for scrotal exploration
audits.setting: District general hospital in Kent (Medway NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Median raphe incision, fixation and closure 100% compliant; orchidopexy in all (100%) non-torsion cases.

audits.intervention: Review in July 2024 with feedback and recommendations for practice.

cycle2.result: Incision, fixation and closure 100% compliant; orchidopexy in non-torsion cases reduced to 75%.

audits.other_findings: Documentation of torsion degree, testicular appearance and follow-up planning stayed inconsistent but improved.
audits.citation: Safdar H, Iftikhar A, Khan N, Algurabi O, Uddin S, Abdulkarim K, et al.. Audit of Compliance With BURST-BAUS FIX-IT Guidelines for Scrotal Exploration in Suspected Testicular Torsion: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study. Cureus. 2025;17(8):e90962. doi:10.7759/cureus.90962. PMID: 41018393.
